architecture.mechanism: Advanced load management strategies — partial loading and selective disconnection of loads — combined with a battery energy storage system to maintain a reliable, stable power supply and prevent charge depletion.
architecture.intervention: Apply vehicle-side load management: selectively disconnect non-essential electrical loads (parasitic drains) when the ignition is off, regulate charging voltage to stabilize the charging bus, and use the battery as a managed energy storage buffer so charge is restored and held rather than drained by standing loads.
architecture.expected_effect: The battery retains charge over parking periods and the charging system maintains voltage stability, eliminating the need for jump starts after replacement.
architecture.falsification_test: With the vehicle at rest, log battery state-of-charge and terminal voltage for 72 hours under two conditions — (a) all loads connected as-is, (b) selective disconnection of non-essential loads plus regulated charge voltage; if condition (b) shows no measurable reduction in discharge rate or still requires a jump start, the mechanism is falsified.
